title: Improving Search Clarification with Structured Information Extracted from Search Results

problem.claim: Conversational search clarification requires generating clarification panes containing candidate aspect items and a clarifying question.

gap.claim: Existing approaches usually rely on unstructured document text and insufficiently use structured information in search results, which can make generated panes inaccurate.

contributions.claim: The paper enhances unstructured documents with an In-List relation extracted from HTML list structures to identify groups of high-quality items with abundant parallel information.
The paper extracts Is-A relations from knowledge bases to support clarification-question generation with explicit prompts.
The paper introduces relation selection to filter ineffective relations and a BART-based model for generating clarification panes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that structured information is a good supplement for generating high-quality clarification panes.

narrative_sequence.summary: Clarification panes in conversational search contain candidate aspect items and a clarifying question.
Existing studies mainly use unstructured document text and may produce inaccurate panes because structured search-result information is not effectively considered.
The paper incorporates In-List relations from HTML lists and Is-A relations from knowledge bases into document information.
Relation selection filters ineffective relations, and a BART-based model generates clarification panes.
The authors report that structured information supports high-quality clarification-pane generation.

source_observation.claim: Search results contain structured relations that can supplement unstructured document text for clarification generation.

interpretation.claim: Representing complementary structure explicitly may improve the information available to a clarification-generation system.

application.claim: When building clarification systems, consider extracting list-based group relations and knowledge-base category relations before generation.

exception.claim: Structured relations may introduce noise, so relation selection or filtering is needed.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the relation-selection criteria or BART training details.
The abstract does not report limitations or independent verification.
